title: Chaos Index
description: SQL-only heuristic scored from 0 to 100 in fixed five-minute buckets. It combines bounded inter-message timing variability (45%), message-length variability (25%), and the share of distinct case/whitespace-normalized messages (30%). At least five messages are required; this is an interpretable disorder proxy, not a canonical statistic.

targets.rawSql:
WITH ordered AS (
  SELECT
    channel_name,
    event_time,
    DATE_BIN(INTERVAL '5 minutes', event_time, TIMESTAMPTZ '2001-01-01 00:00:00+00') AS bucket,
    LENGTH(message)::numeric AS message_length,
    LOWER(REGEXP_REPLACE(BTRIM(message), '[[:space:]]+', ' ', 'g')) AS normalized_message,
    EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM event_time - LAG(event_time) OVER (
      PARTITION BY channel_name
      ORDER BY event_time, id
    ))::numeric AS gap_seconds
  FROM twitch_event_chat
  WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
    AND channel_name IN (${channel:sqlstring})
), components AS (
  SELECT
    channel_name,
    bucket,
    STDDEV_SAMP(gap_seconds) / NULLIF(AVG(gap_seconds), 0) AS arrival_cv,
    STDDEV_SAMP(message_length) / NULLIF(AVG(message_length), 0) AS length_cv,
    COUNT(DISTINCT NULLIF(normalized_message, ''))::numeric / COUNT(*) AS lexical_diversity
  FROM ordered
  GROUP BY channel_name, bucket
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
)
SELECT
  bucket AS time,
  channel_name AS metric,
  ROUND((100.0 * (
    0.45 * COALESCE(arrival_cv / (1.0 + arrival_cv), 0) +
    0.25 * COALESCE(length_cv / (1.0 + length_cv), 0) +
    0.30 * lexical_diversity
  ))::numeric, 2)::double precision AS value
FROM components
ORDER BY time, metric

title: Audience Entropy
description: Normalized Shannon entropy of each channel's per-user message shares over the selected range. Zero means one user produced all messages; 100 means active users contributed equally. Missing user identifiers fall back through username/display name and finally the row id so anonymous rows are not collapsed into one artificial super-user.

targets.rawSql:
WITH user_counts AS (
  SELECT
    channel_name,
    COALESCE(
      NULLIF(user_id, ''),
      NULLIF(user_name, ''),
      NULLIF(display_name, ''),
      'row:' || id::text
    ) AS user_key,
    COUNT(*)::numeric AS messages
  FROM twitch_event_chat
  WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
    AND channel_name IN (${channel:sqlstring})
  GROUP BY channel_name, user_key
), totals AS (
  SELECT
    channel_name,
    COUNT(*) AS users,
    SUM(messages) AS total_messages
  FROM user_counts
  GROUP BY channel_name
), shares AS (
  SELECT
    u.channel_name,
    u.messages / t.total_messages AS p,
    t.users
  FROM user_counts u
  JOIN totals t USING (channel_name)
)
SELECT
  channel_name AS "Channel",
  ROUND(CASE
    WHEN MAX(users) <= 1 THEN 0
    ELSE 100.0 * -SUM(p * LN(p)) / LN(MAX(users)::numeric)
  END, 1) AS "Entropy %"
FROM shares
GROUP BY channel_name
ORDER BY "Entropy %" DESC

title: Raid-Like Influx
description: Candidate five-minute influxes with at least five chatters and at least three times the preceding hour's dense-bucket average. The newcomer share counts users whose first appearance inside the selected range is in that bucket, so this is a raid-like proxy and can overstate newcomers near the range's left boundary.

targets.rawSql:
WITH events AS (
  SELECT
    channel_name,
    DATE_BIN(INTERVAL '5 minutes', event_time, TIMESTAMPTZ '2001-01-01 00:00:00+00') AS bucket,
    COALESCE(
      NULLIF(user_id, ''),
      NULLIF(user_name, ''),
      NULLIF(display_name, ''),
      'row:' || id::text
    ) AS user_key
  FROM twitch_event_chat
  WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
    AND channel_name IN (${channel:sqlstring})
), channels AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT channel_name FROM events
), bounds AS (
  SELECT MIN(bucket) AS first_bucket, MAX(bucket) AS last_bucket FROM events
), grid AS (
  SELECT c.channel_name, gs AS bucket
  FROM channels c
  CROSS JOIN bounds b
  CROSS JOIN LATERAL GENERATE_SERIES(
    b.first_bucket,
    b.last_bucket,
    INTERVAL '5 minutes'
  ) AS gs
), user_first AS (
  SELECT channel_name, user_key, MIN(bucket) AS first_bucket
  FROM events
  GROUP BY channel_name, user_key
), activity AS (
  SELECT
    e.channel_name,
    e.bucket,
    COUNT(DISTINCT e.user_key)::numeric AS chatters,
    COUNT(DISTINCT e.user_key) FILTER (
      WHERE f.first_bucket = e.bucket
    )::numeric AS newcomers
  FROM events e
  JOIN user_first f USING (channel_name, user_key)
  GROUP BY e.channel_name, e.bucket
), dense AS (
  SELECT
    g.channel_name,
    g.bucket,
    COALESCE(a.chatters, 0) AS chatters,
    COALESCE(a.newcomers, 0) AS newcomers
  FROM grid g
  LEFT JOIN activity a USING (channel_name, bucket)
), baselined AS (
  SELECT
    *,
    AVG(chatters) OVER (
      PARTITION BY channel_name
      ORDER BY bucket
      ROWS BETWEEN 12 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
    ) AS baseline_chatters,
    COUNT(*) OVER (
      PARTITION BY channel_name
      ORDER BY bucket
      ROWS BETWEEN 12 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
    ) AS baseline_points
  FROM dense
)
SELECT
  TO_CHAR(bucket AT TIME ZONE '${timezone}', 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI') AS "Local time",
  channel_name AS "Channel",
  chatters::bigint AS "Chatters",
  newcomers::bigint AS "Newcomers",
  ROUND(100.0 * newcomers / NULLIF(chatters, 0), 1) AS "Newcomer %",
  ROUND(chatters / GREATEST(baseline_chatters, 1), 1) AS "Influx multiple"
FROM baselined
WHERE baseline_points >= 6
  AND chatters >= 5
  AND chatters >= 3 * GREATEST(baseline_chatters, 1)
ORDER BY
  (chatters / GREATEST(baseline_chatters, 1)) *
  (newcomers / NULLIF(chatters, 0)) DESC NULLS LAST,
  bucket DESC
LIMIT 25

title: Crowd Synchronization
description: Per-minute share of all messages belonging to an identical normalized-message group used by at least three distinct users. Normalization lowercases, trims, and collapses whitespace; punctuation is preserved to avoid treating merely similar messages as identical.

targets.rawSql:
WITH events AS (
  SELECT
    channel_name,
    DATE_BIN(INTERVAL '1 minute', event_time, TIMESTAMPTZ '2001-01-01 00:00:00+00') AS bucket,
    COALESCE(
      NULLIF(user_id, ''),
      NULLIF(user_name, ''),
      NULLIF(display_name, ''),
      'row:' || id::text
    ) AS user_key,
    NULLIF(
      LOWER(REGEXP_REPLACE(BTRIM(message), '[[:space:]]+', ' ', 'g')),
      ''
    ) AS normalized_message
  FROM twitch_event_chat
  WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
    AND channel_name IN (${channel:sqlstring})
), totals AS (
  SELECT channel_name, bucket, COUNT(*)::numeric AS total_messages
  FROM events
  GROUP BY channel_name, bucket
), repeated_groups AS (
  SELECT
    channel_name,
    bucket,
    normalized_message,
    COUNT(*)::numeric AS repeated_messages,
    COUNT(DISTINCT user_key) AS distinct_users
  FROM events
  WHERE normalized_message IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY channel_name, bucket, normalized_message
), synchronized AS (
  SELECT
    channel_name,
    bucket,
    COALESCE(SUM(repeated_messages) FILTER (WHERE distinct_users >= 3), 0) AS synchronized_messages
  FROM repeated_groups
  GROUP BY channel_name, bucket
)
SELECT
  t.bucket AS time,
  t.channel_name AS metric,
  ROUND((100.0 * COALESCE(s.synchronized_messages, 0) / t.total_messages)::numeric, 2)::double precision AS value
FROM totals t
LEFT JOIN synchronized s USING (channel_name, bucket)
ORDER BY time, metric

title: Silence-to-Explosion Transitions
description: A transition is a minute with at least 10 messages after a fully observed 10-minute baseline containing at most two messages. Missing minutes are generated as zeros. The explosion multiple compares the current minute with the prior per-minute average, floored at 0.1 to keep completely silent baselines finite.

targets.rawSql:
WITH events AS (
  SELECT
    channel_name,
    DATE_BIN(INTERVAL '1 minute', event_time, TIMESTAMPTZ '2001-01-01 00:00:00+00') AS bucket
  FROM twitch_event_chat
  WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
    AND channel_name IN (${channel:sqlstring})
), channels AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT channel_name FROM events
), bounds AS (
  SELECT MIN(bucket) AS first_bucket, MAX(bucket) AS last_bucket FROM events
), grid AS (
  SELECT c.channel_name, gs AS bucket
  FROM channels c
  CROSS JOIN bounds b
  CROSS JOIN LATERAL GENERATE_SERIES(
    b.first_bucket,
    b.last_bucket,
    INTERVAL '1 minute'
  ) AS gs
), counts AS (
  SELECT channel_name, bucket, COUNT(*)::numeric AS messages
  FROM events
  GROUP BY channel_name, bucket
), dense AS (
  SELECT
    g.channel_name,
    g.bucket,
    COALESCE(c.messages, 0) AS messages
  FROM grid g
  LEFT JOIN counts c USING (channel_name, bucket)
), rolling AS (
  SELECT
    *,
    SUM(messages) OVER (
      PARTITION BY channel_name
      ORDER BY bucket
      ROWS BETWEEN 10 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
    ) AS prior_10m_messages,
    COUNT(*) OVER (
      PARTITION BY channel_name
      ORDER BY bucket
      ROWS BETWEEN 10 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
    ) AS baseline_points
  FROM dense
)
SELECT
  TO_CHAR(bucket AT TIME ZONE '${timezone}', 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI') AS "Local time",
  channel_name AS "Channel",
  prior_10m_messages::bigint AS "Prior 10m messages",
  messages::bigint AS "Explosion messages",
  ROUND(messages / GREATEST(prior_10m_messages / 10.0, 0.1), 1) AS "Explosion multiple"
FROM rolling
WHERE baseline_points = 10
  AND prior_10m_messages <= 2
  AND messages >= 10
ORDER BY "Explosion multiple" DESC, bucket DESC
LIMIT 25

title: Channel Heartbeat
description: Inter-message gap summary per channel inside the selected range. Median gap represents the typical pulse, p95 exposes recurring stalls, and maximum gap shows the longest observed silence. The first message has no preceding in-range beat and is excluded from gap statistics.

targets.rawSql:
WITH ordered AS (
  SELECT
    channel_name,
    event_time,
    LAG(event_time) OVER (
      PARTITION BY channel_name
      ORDER BY event_time, id
    ) AS previous_event_time
  FROM twitch_event_chat
  WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
    AND channel_name IN (${channel:sqlstring})
), summary AS (
  SELECT
    channel_name,
    COUNT(*) AS messages,
    MAX(event_time AT TIME ZONE '${timezone}') AS last_local_event
  FROM ordered
  GROUP BY channel_name
), gaps AS (
  SELECT
    channel_name,
    EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM event_time - previous_event_time)::numeric AS gap_seconds
  FROM ordered
  WHERE previous_event_time IS NOT NULL
), gap_stats AS (
  SELECT
    channel_name,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY gap_seconds) AS median_gap,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY gap_seconds) AS p95_gap,
    MAX(gap_seconds) AS max_gap
  FROM gaps
  GROUP BY channel_name
)
SELECT
  s.channel_name AS "Channel",
  s.messages AS "Messages",
  TO_CHAR(s.last_local_event, 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS') AS "Last beat",
  ROUND(g.median_gap::numeric, 1) AS "Median gap (s)",
  ROUND(g.p95_gap::numeric, 1) AS "P95 gap (s)",
  ROUND(g.max_gap::numeric, 1) AS "Max gap (s)"
FROM summary s
LEFT JOIN gap_stats g USING (channel_name)
ORDER BY g.median_gap NULLS LAST, s.channel_name

title: Routine Drift
description: Total-variation distance, scaled 0 to 100, between each channel's local weekly-hour message distribution in the first and second halves of the selected range. Zero means identical routines and 100 means no overlapping active weekly-hour slots. Both halves must contain messages; ranges spanning multiple weeks are most reliable.

targets.rawSql:
WITH bounds AS (
  SELECT
    ($__timeFrom())::timestamptz + (
      (($__timeTo())::timestamptz - ($__timeFrom())::timestamptz) / 2
    ) AS midpoint
), binned AS (
  SELECT
    channel_name,
    CASE WHEN event_time < bounds.midpoint THEN 'earlier' ELSE 'recent' END AS period,
    (
      (EXTRACT(ISODOW FROM event_time AT TIME ZONE '${timezone}')::int - 1) * 24 +
      EXTRACT(HOUR FROM event_time AT TIME ZONE '${timezone}')::int
    ) AS weekly_hour,
    COUNT(*)::numeric AS messages
  FROM twitch_event_chat
  CROSS JOIN bounds
  WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
    AND channel_name IN (${channel:sqlstring})
  GROUP BY channel_name, period, weekly_hour
), totals AS (
  SELECT channel_name, period, SUM(messages) AS total_messages
  FROM binned
  GROUP BY channel_name, period
), shares AS (
  SELECT
    b.channel_name,
    b.weekly_hour,
    b.period,
    b.messages / t.total_messages AS share
  FROM binned b
  JOIN totals t USING (channel_name, period)
), aligned AS (
  SELECT
    channel_name,
    weekly_hour,
    COALESCE(MAX(share) FILTER (WHERE period = 'earlier'), 0) AS earlier_share,
    COALESCE(MAX(share) FILTER (WHERE period = 'recent'), 0) AS recent_share
  FROM shares
  GROUP BY channel_name, weekly_hour
), eligible AS (
  SELECT channel_name
  FROM totals
  GROUP BY channel_name
  HAVING COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE period = 'earlier') = 1
     AND COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE period = 'recent') = 1
)
SELECT
  a.channel_name AS "Channel",
  ROUND(50.0 * SUM(ABS(a.recent_share - a.earlier_share)), 1) AS "Drift %"
FROM aligned a
JOIN eligible e USING (channel_name)
GROUP BY a.channel_name
ORDER BY "Drift %" DESC

title: Top-User Concentration (1% / 5% / 10%)
description: Share of channel messages produced by the highest-volume ceiling of 1%, 5%, and 10% of active users; each tier includes at least one user. Identity falls back through username/display name and finally row id, preventing unidentified rows from becoming one artificial top user.

targets.rawSql:
WITH user_counts AS (
  SELECT
    channel_name,
    COALESCE(
      NULLIF(user_id, ''),
      NULLIF(user_name, ''),
      NULLIF(display_name, ''),
      'row:' || id::text
    ) AS user_key,
    COUNT(*)::numeric AS messages
  FROM twitch_event_chat
  WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
    AND channel_name IN (${channel:sqlstring})
  GROUP BY channel_name, user_key
), ranked AS (
  SELECT
    channel_name,
    user_key,
    messages,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY channel_name
      ORDER BY messages DESC, user_key
    ) AS user_rank,
    COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY channel_name) AS user_count,
    SUM(messages) OVER (PARTITION BY channel_name) AS total_messages
  FROM user_counts
)
SELECT
  channel_name AS "Channel",
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(messages) FILTER (
    WHERE user_rank <= GREATEST(1, CEIL(user_count * 0.01))
  ) / MAX(total_messages), 1) AS "Top 1%",
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(messages) FILTER (
    WHERE user_rank <= GREATEST(1, CEIL(user_count * 0.05))
  ) / MAX(total_messages), 1) AS "Top 5%",
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(messages) FILTER (
    WHERE user_rank <= GREATEST(1, CEIL(user_count * 0.10))
  ) / MAX(total_messages), 1) AS "Top 10%"
FROM ranked
GROUP BY channel_name
ORDER BY "Top 1%" DESC

title: Chat Burst Anomaly Score
description: Positive one-minute burst z-score against the preceding 60 dense one-minute buckets per channel. The denominator is sqrt(trailing variance + 1), which regularizes flat or sparse baselines without infinite scores. At least 10 preceding buckets are required; ordinary and below-baseline minutes display as zero.

targets.rawSql:
WITH events AS (
  SELECT
    channel_name,
    DATE_BIN(INTERVAL '1 minute', event_time, TIMESTAMPTZ '2001-01-01 00:00:00+00') AS bucket
  FROM twitch_event_chat
  WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
    AND channel_name IN (${channel:sqlstring})
), channels AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT channel_name FROM events
), bounds AS (
  SELECT MIN(bucket) AS first_bucket, MAX(bucket) AS last_bucket FROM events
), grid AS (
  SELECT c.channel_name, gs AS bucket
  FROM channels c
  CROSS JOIN bounds b
  CROSS JOIN LATERAL GENERATE_SERIES(
    b.first_bucket,
    b.last_bucket,
    INTERVAL '1 minute'
  ) AS gs
), counts AS (
  SELECT channel_name, bucket, COUNT(*)::numeric AS messages
  FROM events
  GROUP BY channel_name, bucket
), dense AS (
  SELECT
    g.channel_name,
    g.bucket,
    COALESCE(c.messages, 0) AS messages
  FROM grid g
  LEFT JOIN counts c USING (channel_name, bucket)
), baselined AS (
  SELECT
    *,
    AVG(messages) OVER (
      PARTITION BY channel_name
      ORDER BY bucket
      ROWS BETWEEN 60 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
    ) AS baseline_mean,
    VAR_SAMP(messages) OVER (
      PARTITION BY channel_name
      ORDER BY bucket
      ROWS BETWEEN 60 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
    ) AS baseline_variance,
    COUNT(*) OVER (
      PARTITION BY channel_name
      ORDER BY bucket
      ROWS BETWEEN 60 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
    ) AS baseline_points
  FROM dense
)
SELECT
  bucket AS time,
  channel_name AS metric,
  ROUND(GREATEST(
    0,
    (messages - baseline_mean) / SQRT(COALESCE(baseline_variance, 0) + 1)
  ), 2)::double precision AS value
FROM baselined
WHERE baseline_points >= 10
ORDER BY time, metric
